name: Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape
description: This vast stretch of grassland along the Orkhon River in central Mongolia, about 320 km west of Ulaanbaatar, is still grazed by nomadic herders today. Scattered across it are archaeological remains dating back to the 6th century, along with Kharkhorum, the 13th- and 14th-century capital of Genghis Khan's empire. Together they show how roaming pastoralists and their towns and monasteries shaped Central Asian history.
